match: # Web addresses typed into Google Calendar that the site must not link to as they are: a site that was hacked, an old file that moved. Each row is applied to every link of every calendar entry (Web:, Link:, IMG:, the place, addresses in the text and in Note lines) on the pages, in Add to calendar, in the .ics files and in events.json. The calendar check (npm run check:calendar) names each entry that still has such a link, so it can be fixed in Google Calendar too.

# match = a site's name (aadistrict17.info: also matches www.aadistrict17.info and its other sub-sites) or the start of an address, beginning with the site's name (msca09aa.org/wp-content/, not /wp-content/; no * at the end: a row already covers every address that starts with it). Capitals do not matter, and an address hidden inside another one (an Office viewer's ?src=https%3A%2F%2F…) is found too. The first row that matches wins, so put the more precise rows first. replace_with = the full address to link instead (starting with https://); leave it empty to take the link (and the address) off the site. A site's name with an empty replace_with must not appear anywhere on the site: the site check stops if a data/*.csv file still links to it. since = the day the row was added (YYYY-MM-DD). note = why.
